recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for the current build. If ClinicalAssessment is reintroduced as an active core resource, revisit Condition.stage.assessment to decide whether the original FHIR-5804 target list should again include it.
issue_request: FHIR-5804 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request from DSTU1 asking whether Condition.stage.assessment was too broad as Reference(Any). The accepted resolution was to change it to Reference(ClinicalAssessment|DiagnosticReport|Observation).
initial_application: Git history shows the issue was applied by f5d7f1054b, changing the Condition spreadsheet from Reference(Any) to Reference(ClinicalAssessment|DiagnosticReport|Observation). Commit 74daa24071 then replaced ClinicalAssessment with ClinicalImpression after the resource name changed.
additional_context: R4 and R5 publication surfaces included ClinicalImpression alongside DiagnosticReport and Observation. For R6, FHIR-46596 renamed ClinicalImpression back to ClinicalAssessment, and later commit fad1b9cf84 removed ClinicalAssessment from the active resource list and from Condition.stage.assessment. The current local source/fhir.ini has Condition active but no active ClinicalAssessment or ClinicalImpression resource entry, and build.fhir.org reports Condition.stage.assessment targets DiagnosticReport and Observation while clinicalassessment.profile.json returns 404.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the active source already satisfies the core FHIR-5804 concern by avoiding Reference(Any), and reintroducing a target profile for an out-of-build ClinicalAssessment resource would be unsafe for the current build.

related_jiras.note: Renamed ClinicalImpression to ClinicalAssessment before the resource was later removed from the active build, explaining why the original named target is absent now.

evidence_items.learned: The current omission of the clinical assessment target is a later build-scope change, not evidence that FHIR-5804 remains unapplied.
